title: Quitting while on top and entering nursing school in 1954
summary: After Snub Mosley she stopped singing to be remembered at her peak, and the day after her mother died in January 1954 she began nursing school.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: When did the time come when you stopped singing? Did you just suddenly say, 'I'm through singing'?

Yes. When the time came I did well. When I finished with Snub Mosely, I did well the whole time I was in show business, fortunately. I went as far as you could go. I played Broadway. I played the Royal Theater in London. I played the Casino de Paris in Paris and the National in Copenhagen, and the places that were considered the greatest, and I figured I had gone to the top. And my records sold in the millions. So I figured I had gone as far as I could go. And I didn't -- I decided I wasn't going to sing anymore because I didn't want to spoil what I had done. People would come to me and say -- want me to go in a show, and I didn't feel I could do, maybe, justice to what they wanted me to do. And I -- inasmuch as I had made good, I wanted people to remember me --

On top. I didn't want them to say, "Is she still here?" I didn't want that. So, when my mother passed, on January the 17th, 1954, I went to -- started to school the next day, nursing school. I went to the YWCA nursing school on 137th Street, and Phyllis Butts, that was the instructor there, and she accepted me. And I started to school, nursing school. And I was a little old there, you know, but fortunately I left that state board with a marvelous rating.

Yes, I did. And some of the girls who were taking the psychometric test, they couldn't pass it. They flunked it, and they had just come out of high school. And when we were doing the problems on narcotics, I hope to tell you, Miss Southern who was the instructor, had me to get up and work the examples on the narcotics, to show them how they should be done. All right, now.
And I was the oldest one.
And that's when you stopped singing.
